basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Daboque tibi et semini tuo terram peregrinationis tuae omnem terram Chanaan in'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Daboque tibi et semini tuo terram peregrinationis tuae omnem terram Chanaan in possessionem aeternam. Operosiore expositione indiget quomodo accipiatur impletum, sive adhuc exspectetur implendum, cum possessio quaecunque terrena, aeterna cuilibet genti esse non possit. Sed sciendum est aeternum a nostris interpretari quod Graeci appellant Aeonion, quod a saeculo derivatum est. Aeon quippe Graece seculum nuncupatur. Sed non ausi Latini hoc dicere saeculare, ne longe in aliud mitterent sensum. Saecularia quippe dicuntur multa quae in hoc saeculo sic aguntur, sicut brevi etiam tempore transeant. Aeonion autem quod dicitur, aut non habet finem, aut usque in hujus saeculi tenditur finem. Et ideo, sicut et supra diximus, terra Chanaan in possessionem aeternam semini datur Abrahae, quoniam in ea Christiani usque ad finem saeculi hujus, sive de Judaeis, sive de gentibus, semen videlicet Abrahae nunquam defuturi esse creduntur.
